title: Progressive degradation exposure and adaptive throttle observability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We've observed tenant-visible progressive degradation during regional congestion events where token-level latency climbs before the admit-rate controller engages. Current dashboards surface p95/p99 at request level but do not attribute degradation slices to token positions, region failovers, or per-tenant admit decisions. This ticket builds instrumentation and a dashboard layer to expose progressive degradation signals and tie them to adaptive throttling and circuit states for faster diagnosis and safer rollouts.

Scope:
- Add token-level timing histograms (position-aware) with tenant and region labels.
- Emit admit_score/admit_decision metrics at ingress and attach shard/route metadata.
- Register circuit_state transitions (OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED) per-region and per-priority-path.
- Surface derived SLO SLIs: token_p50/p95/p99 latency, token_kv_cache_hit_ratio, tenant_admit_rate, region_fallback_count, circuit_state_ratio.
- Build an operational dashboard (panels listed below) and a small synthetic harness to validate signal correctness.

Instrumentation details (implementation notes):
- Token timing: instrument the decode loop to record per-token durations into histograms bucketed at ms resolution. Label dims: tenant_id, model_family, region, shard_id, token_position_bucket (0-15,16-63,64+), route_priority. Keep cardinality low by truncating tenant_id to org_id.
- Admit metrics: emit admit_total{decision="admit"} and admit_total{decision="reject"} with tenant/org labels. Also emit admit_score gauge per request for sampling.
- KV cache: export kv_cache_requests and kv_cache_hits with model_family + region to calculate hit ratio.
- Circuit transitions: emit circuit_transitions_total{state="OPEN"|"HALF_OPEN"|"CLOSED",region=..,path=..}. Also emit circuit_active{region, path} gauge.
- Sampling: for high-volume tenants sample token histograms at 1/100 and provide full sampling for tenants flagged in .whitelist for initial validation.

Suggested example queries (PromQL-style) for dashboard panels:
- Token p95 (position 0-15): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket{token_position_bucket="0-15"}[5m])) by (le, tenant_id, region))
- KV cache hit ratio: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) by (model_family, region) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[5m])) by (model_family, region)
- Tenant admit rate: sum(rate(admit_total{decision="admit"}[5m])) by (tenant_id) / sum(rate(admit_total{decision!=""}[5m])) by (tenant_id)
- Region fallback count: increase(region_fallback_events[1h]) by (region)

Dashboard panels to build:
1) Progressive token-latency waterfall: stacked view by token_position_bucket and tenant cohorts.
2) Tenant admit-rate heatmap sorted by traffic-weighted latency impact.
3) Circuit state timeline per-region and per-priority-path (interactive to jump to traces).
4) KV cache heatmap and its correlation with token p95 over time.
5) Synthetic-run comparison panel: baseline vs degraded run showing admit metrics and latencies.
6) SLO surface: tenant-level burn-rate with links to runbook and auto-run remediation checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- New metrics are emitted in prod telemetry pipeline within low-cardinality constraints.
- Dashboard panels implemented in Grafana and wire up to alerting rules.
- Synthetic harness can reproduce a progressive degradation scenario and dashboards reflect expected signals (p95 climb, admit_rate drop, circuit OPEN transitions).
- On-call runbook updated with steps: interpret heatmap, trigger holdback for specific tenant, escalate to SRE and product.
- No more than 5% added ingestion cost for global telemetry (validated by telemetry budget dashboard).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): instrument on canary region with full sampling for 5 tenants (2 days), validate correctness (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Phase 2 (staged): enable sampled histograms globally (1/100) + admit metrics; run synthetic at peak window to validate (owner: Leah Nguyen).
- Phase 3 (GA): increase sampling for top-20 tenants gradually and enable dashboard alerts.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cardinality blowup: mitigate by truncating tenant_id and bucketing positions. Add quota guard in ingestion pipeline.
- Perf overhead: token timing is cheap but avoid nanosecond-precision across all hot paths; use sampling and efficient histograms.
- Mis-attribution during multi-region failover: ensure region and fallback_reason tags are present on fallback events.

- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Progressive+Degradation+Observability (draft)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128 (WIP)
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/xyz/progressive-degradation (prototype)
